newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Greens launch web site for draft laws.
newsitem.headline: German Greens launch web site for draft laws.

text.p: Germany's Greens on Tuesday opened an Internet site aimed at sounding out reaction to draft legislation and started by posting a proposed law on railways.
The Greens Party invited people to visit the web site, where they have posted their new railway bill, to start a debate on transport policy.
"Replies will be very welcome," said Greens railways spokesman Ali Schmidt in a statement.
"We are proposing a second railway reform to promote more competition at Deutsche Bahn AG -- which is still a monopoly -- and to make it more ecologically sound," said Schmidt.
Germany last reformed its railways in 1994. The reform included the merging of the national rail companies of former East and West Germany. But Schmidt said those changes had not gone far enough.

Schmidt said Germany's rail and bus services should be modernised, and trains and stations made more customer-friendly. He said the Greens also wanted to minimise further noise pollution along Germany's railway lines.
